item.title: 911 Calls Detail How Keefe D’s Lawyer Michael Sanft Was Found Dead
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Two employees' calls to 911 reveal what happened inside attorney Michael Sanft's Las Vegas home after one went upstairs.
item.content:encoded:
Keefe D‘s lawyer Michael Sanft was found dead by two of his employees at his Las Vegas condo on the morning of November 6. In 911 recordings obtained by TMZ, one employee can be heard offering to take over the call as his coworker struggles to tell a dispatcher what happened.

“We had not heard from our boss for a few days, so we came to his house to check on him,” the man told the dispatcher. The caller said he found the 55-year-old attorney on his bed upstairs, then told the dispatcher, “He’s not alive.”

It was the woman who first reached 911 from the condo in the Las Vegas Country Club community. The dispatcher asked her to stay on the line, but she hung up. When her coworker called back, she could still be heard crying as he told the dispatcher he didn’t think Sanft could be revived.

Clark County Fire Department dispatch records put the first call at about 7:04 a.m. An ambulance went out two minutes later and reached the home around 7:16 a.m. The Clark County coroner had not released a cause of death when the recordings became public on November 20.

A week before his employees found him, Sanft had filed notice that Keefe D would appeal his conviction for Tupac Shakur’s murder. The Las Vegas attorney took the case without charging Keefe D and led his defense at trial in August.

Prosecutors used Keefe D’s own accounts of the 1996 shooting to argue that he supplied the gun after Shakur and others fought his nephew Orlando Anderson at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Sanft argued that his client had embellished the story in interviews and a memoir to make money, and that police couldn’t independently confirm key details.

The defense called three former Las Vegas police officers, but Keefe D didn’t testify. Jurors deliberated for less than three hours on August 31 before convicting him of first-degree murder. Judge Carli Kierny sentenced him to 40 years to life on October 13.

The Nevada Supreme Court opened the appeal on November 9 and gave the defense 120 days to file its first written argument.

item.title: The Notorious B.I.G. Sets A Premiere For His YouTube Station
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The Notorious B.I.G. brings a new broadcast to the YouTube channel that also hosts Angie Martinez's series on his second album.
item.content:encoded:
The Notorious B.I.G. has a YouTube station set to premiere on the channel that houses his music videos. The first broadcast is scheduled for noon Eastern on Wednesday, November 25.

Viewers can join the chat on the official livestream page before the broadcast begins. An introduction on the page reads, “You’re Watching the Official Station of the Greatest to Ever Do It. All Biggie. All The Time.”

Among the videos on the channel are “Juicy” and “Big Poppa,” two singles from Biggie’s 1994 debut, Ready to Die. “Big Poppa” reached No. 6 on the Hot 100 and topped the rap and R&B charts. The Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry in 2024, nearly 30 years after its release.

That’s the same catalog Biggie’s estate began restoring for YouTube in 2022. On the 25th anniversary of Life After Death, the estate teamed up with Bad Boy, Rhino and Atlantic to bring 4K versions of his official videos to the channel.

The anniversary project also brought remastered versions of the album and its singles back to vinyl, including the original 12-inch releases of “Hypnotize” and “Sky’s the Limit.”

The channel later turned from the music videos to how Life After Death came together. Biggie’s second album arrived in March 1997, weeks after he was killed in Los Angeles.

Angie Martinez returned to that record in 2023 for Iconic Records, an eight-episode series that ran on Biggie’s official YouTube channel as well as on Roku.

Biggie manager Wayne Barrow described why the series depended on people who knew the rapper and worked with him.

“His work has been examined and reviewed before, but this series provides new stories and firsthand accounts by the people that were there,” Barrow said when WMX announced the series.

Martinez talked to producers and rappers who could explain how individual songs came together. In the episode about “Notorious Thugs,” Fat Joe said he helped bring Biggie and Bone Thugs-N-Harmony together, while Lil Cease and Layzie Bone revisited the California recording session. Another episode brought in Buckwild to talk about producing “I Got a Story to Tell.”

“Hypnotize” became the first single of Biggie’s career to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

item.title: YouTube Brought Warner Music Group Roughly $1 Billion In Annual Revenue
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: YouTube accounted for 14% of Warner Music Group's annual revenue, up from 12% a year earlier, according to its SEC filing.
item.content:encoded:
Warner Music Group took in roughly $1 billion in revenue from YouTube in its latest fiscal year. The platform accounted for 14% of Warner’s business, up from 12% the year before, putting it ahead of Apple and behind Spotify among the music company’s biggest customers.

Warner’s annual filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission reports total revenue of $7.437 billion for the year ended September 30. Applying YouTube’s rounded share to that total gives an estimate of $1.04 billion, compared with about $805 million the previous year.

Spotify accounted for 21% of revenue this time, up from 20% a year earlier, while Apple’s share fell from 11% to 10%. Together, the three platforms accounted for about 45% of Warner’s revenue, up from 43%. Warner’s total annual revenue rose to $6.707 billion.

The numbers include both the company’s record-label and music-publishing businesses. Those are two different sets of rights: the label side handles recordings, while the publishing side administers the underlying songs.

The filing doesn’t break out what YouTube revenue came from specific artists or what any of them received. It also gives no split between subscription and advertising revenue for the platform.

A multi-year Spotify agreement announced last year covered both recordings and publishing. It let Warner Chappell license songs directly to Spotify in more countries, including the United States.

YouTube’s share of Warner revenue had held at 12% in both 2024 and 2025, while Spotify’s share climbed from 18% to 20%.

YouTube’s global head of music, Lyor Cohen, said the platform paid more than $8 billion to the music industry from July 2024 through June 2025, combining advertising and subscription revenue.

That is an industry-wide figure for a different period, not the amount Warner booked from YouTube.

“Our agreements with digital music services generally last one to three years,” Warner wrote in the filing.

It said it expects its licenses with the three platforms to renew as usual, while warning that lower platform pricing or a decline in royalty rates could cut into its revenue.

item.title: Eminem’s Manager Reveals How Wu-Tang Beat Out Other Acts For Thanksgiving
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Paul Rosenberg recalls pitching Wu-Tang Clan to the Detroit Lions and leaves one question about Eminem's Thanksgiving unanswered.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem and his manager Paul Rosenberg had three or four acts in mind for Thanksgiving before Wu-Tang Clan pulled ahead.

Coming off a Detroit Lions halftime show built around Jack White’s guitar, the two wanted to hear Hip-Hop at Ford Field this year.

In an interview with Adam Graham of The Detroit News, Rosenberg traced the choice back to conversations that started in the spring.

The Staten Island crew had a tour on the books and a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ahead of them.

The people putting the show together agreed on Wu-Tang before taking their pick to the Lions. Rosenberg wasn’t sure the front office would go along with it, but the team backed the booking.

“The idea of a Wu-Tang Thanksgiving seems so awesome that we went for it,” Rosenberg said.

Bringing a New York group to Ford Field also left room for someone who grew up rooting for Detroit.

Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith will play with Wu-Tang, a reunion for musicians who worked together on a remix in 2000. Smith, who played on that track with guitarist Tom Morello, grew up in Bloomfield Hills and has already played the stadium with the Lions’ own drumline during a playoff game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Rosenberg wouldn’t say whether Eminem would trade his producer’s role for a microphone during Wu-Tang’s set.

Last Thanksgiving, Eminem walked out during White’s set against the Green Bay Packers and rapped over a mix of his own “‘Till I Collapse” and the White Stripes’ “Hello Operator.”

White and Eminem worked out that arrangement at Detroit’s Majestic Theater during the week of the game.

What started as a live collaboration became a single, but Rosenberg said audiences shouldn’t count on seeing his client take the field every Thanksgiving.

This year CBS will carry the Lions’ game against the Chicago Bears at 1 p.m. Eastern on November 26.

It’s the second Thanksgiving under a deal that gives Eminem and Rosenberg a hand in choosing performers and producing the shows through 2027.

As for extending the deal, Rosenberg said, “We haven’t talked about anything beyond next year.”

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: The-Dream Asks Judge To Clarify What Sexual Assault Claim Can Go To Trial
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The-Dream and Contra Paris asked a federal judge to clarify a sealed ruling or throw out the civil sexual assault claim.
item.content:encoded:
The-Dream wants to know what a jury could hear in a civil sexual assault case against him.

He and his label, Contra Paris, asked Judge Sherilyn Peace Garnett in a November 24 filing to clear up what their lawyers describe as a contradiction in a sealed ruling.

That November 10 ruling granted part of a defense request to decide claims without a trial and denied part of it.

The defense says one paragraph ruled in its favor on whether singer Channii Monroe could base her claim on being misled about the purpose of sex, while the next left open a sexual battery claim under a part of California law the lawyers say depends on the same issue.

“The two paragraphs cannot both be given effect as written,” the defense wrote.

The defense says the ruling covers two allegations from February 2015, both of which The-Dream denies. Monroe testified that he placed her hand on his genitals at a Los Angeles recording studio. She said that during a later encounter he ejaculated inside her after she asked him not to.

If Garnett intended to leave the claim open under a different part of the law, the lawyers want her to rule for them on the entire count.

They argue neither alleged act falls under the version of the sexual battery law in force at the time, and they also asked Garnett to correct the ruling’s reference to a statute that sets the time limit for filing suit.

In her June 2024 lawsuit, Monroe alleges that The-Dream used promises of a recording career to control and sexually assault her.

The producer has denied the allegations of sexual assault and abuse. Sony Music Entertainment was also named in the case, but Garnett dismissed the claims against the company in November 2025 and barred Monroe from bringing those claims again in the suit.

A trial date wasn’t confirmed in the latest filing. Garnett cleared the old dates in July and directed both sides to propose a new schedule after she ruled on the defense’s request to decide the case without trial. The two sides asked on November 20 for more time to propose those dates.

The defense’s notice lists a hearing on its request for January 6, 2027, at 1:30 p.m. in Los Angeles.

item.title: Chrisean Rock Asks Viewers To Stop Bullying Her After Blueface Clips
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chrisean Rock pushes back against insults about her parenting as clips of Blueface's criticism keep showing up online.
item.content:encoded:
Chrisean Rock wants people watching her life online to stop tearing her down over it.

The rapper cried on Kick as she addressed attacks on her parenting and described what it was like to keep seeing clips of Blueface criticizing her.

Rock spoke from bed early Tuesday, November 24, during a livestream on her Kick channel.

She questioned who she might have become if she’d never met Blueface, the father of her son. “I just need him to leave me alone,” she said.

Rock said she needed to be mentally present for their son and accused Blueface of telling other streamers not to work with her. She also pushed back on the idea that those disputes would stop her from finding people to work with, saying there were bigger collaborations she could pursue.

Rock also asked viewers to stop bullying her and said she felt scared. “They think I’m strong, they think I’m tough. I had enough,” she said.

As Rock asked the audience to back off, she told them, “This is my cry out for help.”

The attacks Rock described followed her from Kick onto X. The first clip drew more than 449,000 views, and some users responding directly to it mocked her for crying or made the same kinds of judgments about her parenting that she’d just spoken out against.

Rock had addressed public scrutiny over her parenting before this week’s livestream.

Rock and Blueface have shared moments about their relationship on Kick as well as their family life.

In October, he got down on one knee at Problem Lounge in Scottsdale, Arizona, where a sign asked Rock to marry him and people in the club filmed her leaning in to embrace him.

After the engagement ended, Rock talked about where she was putting her energy instead. In an interview while training for a fight, she said her faith and the work she was doing in the gym took priority over whether Blueface supported her.

In a separate piece of the November stream posted to X, Rock said she was reluctant to go live from her house because she didn’t want people knowing where she lived.

item.title: Post Malone’s Nashville Bar Offers Free Thanksgiving Meals To Workers On Duty
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Posty's and Jason Aldean's bar will serve free meals to on-duty first responders and healthcare workers from November 25 to 27.
item.content:encoded:
Post Malone‘s Nashville bar is offering Thanksgiving meals to people working through the holiday. Posty’s and the neighboring Jason Aldean’s Kitchen + Rooftop Bar will cover meals up to $30 for on-duty first responders and healthcare workers from Wednesday, November 25, through Friday, November 27.

Workers should arrive in uniform or scrubs, Nashville’s WZTV reported. The allowance applies to the regular menu or a special Thanksgiving menu at either restaurant. The meals are available for dine-in or takeout.

The two restaurants are next door to each other downtown: Posty’s is at 305 Broadway and Aldean’s is at 307 Broadway. Both will open at 11 a.m. local time on Thanksgiving Day and keep their regular hours on Wednesday and Friday.

The bars made a similar Thanksgiving offer in 2025, when on-duty first responders could get a meal for the same $30 limit. Last year’s announcement named first responders. The offer this week explicitly includes healthcare staff, too.

The restaurants made a separate offer over Christmas last year. The group told WSMV it would cover up to $30 for uniformed first responders working between December 23 and 26.

Post opened the bar with TC Restaurant Group, which also operates Aldean’s Nashville spot. “Nashville has really become a second home for me so I can’t wait to invite y’all over to my house,” he said when the partnership was announced.

Posty’s opened in July 2025. The rapper later marked the grand opening with a free October concert on Broadway after cutting the ribbon with Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell and Metro Police Chief John Drake. Inside, the 26,000-square-foot venue has three stages and a full-service dining room.

The Nashville venture followed F-1 Trillion, Post’s first country album. The album paired him with Morgan Wallen on “I Had Some Help” and with Dolly Parton on “Have the Heart,” according to his official track listing.

Post Malone has used his platform to help frontline workers before. In 2020, he pledged $1 million to charities and asked fans to suggest where it should go. The causes he named included groups helping frontline responders during the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Druski Hosts Chicago’s New Year’s Eve Show: When Free Tickets Drop
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Free Navy Pier tickets for Druski's New Year's Eve show drop November 25 at 10 a.m. Central, with a second round December 2.
item.content:encoded:
Druski will host the New Year’s Eve show at Navy Pier. The first free seats for the live show go up on November 25 at 10 A.M. Central.

Chicago will put out a second batch at the same time on Wednesday, December 2.

Each person can reserve up to two seats through Chicago’s event page, and the tickets will go in the order people claim them. Anyone younger than 18 must come with a parent or legal guardian.

Ticket holders can enter Crystal Gardens at 600 E. Grand Ave. starting at 6 p.m. on December 31, an hour before the music begins. The city is reserving a raised viewing area for guests who use seated mobility devices and asks for at least 72 hours’ notice for access requests.

The audience inside Crystal Gardens may appear on camera when Druski hosts Chicago’s live segments of ABC’s Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve with Ryan Seacrest 2027. “Chicago knows how to put on a show, and this New Year’s Eve will be no exception,” Mayor Brandon Johnson said in announcing the event.

Chicago has booked DJ Mike P, Opal Staples and Isaiah Sharkey for the indoor stage, along with the 911 Mambo Orchestra and house producer Steve “Silk” Hurley. One name is still under wraps: The city says a Grammy winner will headline.

Fans who miss out on a ticket can still spend the night at the pier. Local acts start playing at 6 P.M., and screens will show the indoor set with captions and sign language.

At midnight, the pier will put on a free drone and fireworks show over Lake Michigan.

A separate free fireworks show will light up the Chicago River at midnight. Those fireworks will go off from bridges between Franklin Street and Columbus Drive.

Chance the Rapper led the city’s first ABC countdown last year from a stage by the Chicago River. That show drew fans to the Riverwalk without tickets. This year, the ticket rules apply only to the indoor part of the night at the pier.

Fans who want to stay home can watch the ABC broadcast starting at 7 P.M. Central and 8 P.M. Eastern.

item.title: Kelly Rowland Joins Hulu’s Reasonable Doubt After Surprise Finale
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kelly Rowland joins Season 5 of Hulu's Reasonable Doubt after showing up in the finale as a campaign aide who needs help.
item.content:encoded:
Kelly Rowland will return for the fifth season of Hulu’s Reasonable Doubt after a brief appearance in the fourth-season finale.

The Destiny’s Child singer plays Demitra, a mayoral campaign aide with blood on her hands and a lawyer to find.

That scene closes out “Moment of Clarity,” which began streaming Tuesday, November 24.

Deadline confirmed she’ll return, but it isn’t known whether she’ll be a series regular or have a recurring role.

Demitra approaches defense attorney Jax Stewart, played by Emayatzy Corinealdi, and Krystal, played by Angela Grovey, and asks for help before either can learn what happened.

“If you’re going to ambush anybody, it’s going to be Jax Stewart because my hands are dirty. Literally,” Rowland said in an interview with Forbes.

The scene was a second chance for Rowland to get on the show.

Creator Raamla Mohamed Hunter told Forbes that she’d seen Rowland audition for a different part in the first season and remembered what she could do.

For Demitra, Hunter asked Rowland to take off the makeup she’d arrived in, and Rowland said she trusted the call.

The lawyer Demitra turns to has just finished defending R&B mogul Eric Cropper, played by Tank, and is preparing to split her time between Los Angeles and San Francisco.

The move is for her husband Lewis, played by McKinley Freeman, who has a new job at a tech startup in Northern California.

The fourth season also starred Meagan Good, with guest spots from Morris Chestnut and La La Anthony. Kerry Washington, one of the executive producers, had urged Rowland to take the part.

Hulu renewed the show before viewers met Demitra in what the company says was the series’ most-watched season. The service said audiences had streamed more than 150 million hours across Hulu and Disney+ worldwide.

The latest episode when Hulu announced the renewal drew over 40% more first-day views than the season premiere, according to the service.

The scene outside a law firm gives Rowland a different kind of workplace role after Relationship Goals, the Prime Video film in which she and Method Man played exes vying for the same television job.

Hulu hasn’t announced a premiere date for the fifth season.

item.title: YNW Melly Wins Ruling Blocking Evidence From March 2024 Searches
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: A Broward judge granted YNW Melly's request to block evidence from March 2024 search warrants ahead of his murder retrial.
item.content:encoded:
YNW Melly won a ruling that keeps evidence from March 2024 searches out of his double-murder retrial.

Broward Circuit Judge Martin Fein granted the defense motion, according to courtroom footage posted by journalist Meghann Cuniff.

The ruling covers evidence from an iPhone and from Instagram, Snapchat and Google accounts obtained through those warrants. The judge who signed them had not been told about an earlier ruling on evidence or that both sides had appealed parts of it, Fein said.

Had he known about that earlier ruling, Fein said he would not have signed the warrants.

“But at least at this point, the motion to suppress is granted in full,” he said in court.

A prosecutor said the state had waited for an appeals court decision before disclosing the warrants.

Melly’s lawyers argued that did not explain why the prior ruling was left out of the applications. Fein said he would put his ruling in writing.

The decision prosecutors were waiting for came on October 15, 2025, when Florida’s Fourth District Court of Appeal upheld Judge John Murphy’s limits on the earlier searches.

Prosecutors hadn’t defended the warrants as written. They argued that investigators would have found the evidence anyway or obtained it elsewhere, while Melly’s lawyers wanted all the evidence from those warrants thrown out.

Murphy had examined more than a dozen warrants, including one for a cloud account linked to Melly’s iPhone X. Detectives wanted to know where Melly was around the time of the killings, but neither their application nor the warrant gave a date range.

Murphy allowed five categories of evidence from that account and limited each to the shooting and the few hours on either side.

The ruling does not decide what will happen to evidence tied to Melly’s lyrics, alleged gang ties or alibi. Those disputes concern other evidence prosecutors want jurors to hear at the retrial.

Melly has pleaded not guilty to two first-degree murder charges in the October 2018 deaths of Christopher Thomas Jr. and Anthony Williams.

The first trial ended without a verdict in July 2023 after jurors could not agree.

Jury selection for the retrial remains on the calendar for January 6, 2027.
